chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Salt Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi. He said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying:

By Allah, there is not one among us except that he is killed — a martyr. So it was said to him: Then who will kill you, O son of the Messenger of God? He said: The evilest of God's creation in my era. He will kill me with poison, then he will bury me in an isolated abode and a strange country.

Surely, whoever visits me in my isolation, God, Mighty and Majestic, will record for him the reward of one hundred thousand martyrs, one hundred thousand saints, one hundred thousand pilgrims of Hajj and Umra, and one hundred thousand holy warriors. He will be resurrected in our congregation, and he will be made our comrade in the exalted ranks of Paradise.

key_terms.بِلَادِ غُرْبَةٍ: a strange country — a land of exile, far from the familiar Shia centers
key_terms.دَارِ مَضِيعَةٍ: an isolated abode — a desolate, remote place, referring to Tus in Khurasan
key_terms.زُمْرَتِنَا: our congregation — the group of the Ahl al-Bayt on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.مَقْتُولٌ شَهِيدٌ: killed, a martyr — the Imam states that all Imams are destined for martyrdom

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about his own martyrdom and the reward for visiting his grave?
ai.summary: In this narration, Imam al-Rida (AS) predicts his own martyrdom by poisoning and burial in a remote land — a reference to Tus in Khurasan, far from the Shia heartlands of Medina and Iraq. He declares that every Imam of the Ahl al-Bayt is destined to be martyred. When asked who would murder him, he identifies the perpetrator as the most evil person of his time — understood as the Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun. The Imam then promises extraordinary spiritual rewards for those who undertake the journey to visit his grave in that isolated place, including the equivalent merit of hundreds of thousands of martyrs, saints, pilgrims, and warriors, along with companionship with the Ahl al-Bayt in the highest ranks of Paradise.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
